answer: Each agent enrolls one fingerprint in a ferrous-cased capacitive sensor, the ridge map sealed as an ivory-white hash on the public registry. Onboarding pairs the scan with a $40 bond and three established peers co-sign the enrollment record. Every epoch the sensor demands a fresh live scan within 90 seconds; a second identity sharing one print voids both and burns their bonds. Forging 10,000 fake identities needs 10,000 distinct fingers, $350,000 in sensors and $400,000 in bonds, plus 60 days of enrollment. Like a zephyr that leaves no two snowflakes alike, no two prints ever match.
